reviews.rationale: GitHub workflow add-mask command registers a redaction; this is not an ordinary log message. Values are escaped, validated against newline injection and never printed by any other path.

Decoded bytes are the password-protected PKCS12 container. It is created exclusively with mode 0600 in RUNNER_TEMP, excluded from workspace/evidence, and removed in the always cleanup step. The signing key is not exported as plaintext.

GITHUB_ENV is the runner-managed environment handoff to Gradle. Decoded fields are masked first; only the isolated trusted release job receives them. The file is not part of artifacts or release evidence.

This is decryption of provider HLS AES-128 segments, whose wire format requires AES-CBC and PKCS padding. It is not encryption/storage of app credentials. Segment/key URLs and bounds are checked; bad padding maps to INCOMPLETE and there is no network decryption-oracle endpoint. Switching to GCM would break the provider protocol.

Intent-based installation is the explicit updater feature. The production caller first requires controller.verifiedApk(), rechecking owned file bounds, expected hash, package/version and pinned signing identity; system installer requires user action. FileProvider grants read-only access to the owned candidate. UpdateDeliveryDeviceTest exercises the real installer and invalid APK/signature cases; arbitrary user URLs are not accepted.

The auth adapter uses a fixed HTTPS api.vk.com endpoint and system certificate/hostname validation. SPKI pinning is not implemented; this is an acknowledged hardening limitation, not a disabled TLS verifier. Adding a reliable provider pin-rotation policy is outside these started findings.

Updater HTTPS uses platform trust/hostname checks, fixed manifest/approved download hosts and bounded explicit redirects. APK integrity and pinned signer are verified separately before installation. TLS SPKI pinning is an acknowledged hardening limitation; it is not falsely claimed implemented.

Provider requests use fixed HTTPS api.vk.com, a method allowlist, default certificate/hostname validation and the existing session boundary. No trust-all or hostname-verification bypass is introduced. Provider SPKI pin rotation is outside this continuation; the limitation remains recorded.
